name: General SaaS
description: The cross-cutting product layer every B2B SaaS application needs on top of its vertical features: tenancy and workspaces, onboarding, plans and entitlements, usage metering, team invites, API keys, webhooks, an internal admin console, status/changelog communication, enterprise SSO/SCIM, data export, and feature flags.

sources.title: BoxyHQ SaaS Starter Kit
sources.notes: Verified from repo LICENSE file (Apache-2.0) by an earlier session. Prisma schema: Team (tenant), TeamMember, Invitation, ApiKey, Subscription/Price/Service (billing). Webhooks via svix (pages/api/teams/[slug]/webhooks), SSO via BoxyHQ Jackson SAML (lib/jackson, pages/api/teams/[slug]/sso.ts), SCIM directory sync via Jackson dsync (pages/api/scim/v2.0/[...directory].ts), audit log via Retraced (lib/retraced.ts). No onboarding wizard, no platform-wide admin console/impersonation, no rate limiting found in this repo (checked by grep).

sources.title: NextCRM
sources.notes: Cited here only for its ApiKeys model (prisma model ApiKeys: scope, provider, encryptedKey, per-user) as a second, independent API-key-management implementation. NextCRM is single-tenant (no Team/workspace model) so it does not inform tenancy/invite features.

sources.title: Chatwoot
sources.license: MIT (core; content under enterprise/ is under a separate Chatwoot Enterprise commercial license per LICENSE)
sources.notes: Verified license from repo LICENSE file via `gh api` (core MIT, enterprise/ carved out separately) and confirmed the specific files cited below are outside enterprise/, so are core MIT; reference-only, never copy code. Inspected file tree and file contents remotely (no clone): app/controllers/api/v1/accounts/onboardings_controller.rb + app/services/onboarding/web_widget_creation_service.rb (onboarding), app/models/webhook.rb (account-scoped webhook with url/secret/subscriptions, belongs_to :account), app/controllers/super_admin/* + app/models/super_admin.rb + app/javascript/dashboard/composables/useImpersonation.js + components/app/ImpersonationBanner.vue (internal cross-tenant admin console with a real user-impersonation path), app/javascript/dashboard/api/auditLogs.js + helper/auditlogHelper.js (workspace-facing audit log viewer UI), app/javascript/dashboard/api/customRole.js (custom roles UI), app/javascript/dashboard/api/changelog.js + components-next/changelog-card/* + SidebarChangelogButton.vue (in-app changelog feed with unread indicator), config/initializers/rack_attack.rb (per-account_id and per-API-token throttles on API endpoints, e.g. contacts/search and reports routes).

Inspected file tree remotely: openmeter/ent/db/meter.go, openmeter/billing/featuremeter/** — a second, independent usage-metering implementation alongside Lago.

features.name: Workspace management
features.description: Create, rename, and switch between tenant workspaces; manage workspace-level settings and branding.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: boxyhq's Team prisma model + settings routes, and Twenty CRM's packages/twenty-front/.../modules/settings/workspace/** workspace-settings module (its product's tenant concept is literally named 'Workspace'). Raised the single-source medium to a properly two-sourced medium.

features.name: Guided onboarding
features.description: A first-run setup wizard that walks a new workspace owner through initial configuration after signup.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations found this pass: Chatwoot's onboardings_controller.rb + onboarding/web_widget_creation_service.rb (MIT core), and Twenty CRM's packages/twenty-front/.../modules/onboarding/** (AGPL, reference-only). boxyhq-saas-starter was checked and confirmed NOT to have an onboarding wizard, so it is not cited as evidence. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Team invites
features.description: Invite people to a workspace by email with a pre-assigned role; manage pending, accepted, and expired invitations.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: boxyhq's Invitation prisma model + invite routes, and Twenty CRM's packages/twenty-front/.../modules/workspace-invitation/** (sendInvitations, resendWorkspaceInvitation, deleteWorkspaceInvitation). Raised the single-source medium to a properly two-sourced medium. Still depends on shared.users for the underlying account mechanics.

features.name: Plans and entitlements
features.description: Subscription plan tiers with feature gating and usage/seat limits enforced per workspace.

provenance.notes: boxyhq: Subscription/Price/Service prisma models (Stripe-backed plan tiers). Lago (reference-only, AGPL): explicit Plan + Entitlement + Wallet models. Two independent implementations = medium.

features.name: Usage metering
features.description: Record usage events (API calls, seats, storage, etc.) per workspace to drive limits, alerts, and usage-based billing.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: Lago's BillableMetric/Event/DailyUsage models and OpenMeter's Meter entity (openmeter/ent/db/meter.go) plus its billing/featuremeter module — OpenMeter's own description is literally 'usage-based billing' metering. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: API keys
features.description: Issue and revoke scoped API keys per workspace for programmatic access, with prefix display and last-used tracking.

provenance.notes: boxyhq: ApiKey prisma model scoped to a Team, with routes under pages/api/teams/[slug]/. NextCRM: separate ApiKeys model (per-user, per-provider) — a different flavor (storing third-party keys vs issuing the product's own keys) but the same underlying entity/feature shape. Two independent implementations = medium.

features.name: Outbound webhooks
features.description: Let a workspace subscribe to product events and receive signed HTTP callbacks, with delivery retry and a delivery log.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: boxyhq's Svix-backed team webhook endpoints, and Chatwoot's app/models/webhook.rb (account-scoped, url/secret/subscriptions, MIT core). Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Internal admin console
features.description: An internal, staff-only console for searching tenants, viewing account health, impersonating a tenant user for support purposes, and taking other cross-tenant support actions.

provenance.notes: Chatwoot's app/controllers/super_admin/** + app/models/super_admin.rb + useImpersonation.js/ImpersonationBanner.vue (MIT core) is a real, verified internal cross-tenant console with a genuine support-impersonation path, corroborating what was previously only a reasoned SOC 2 inference. One implementation + one authoritative standard = medium. Description updated to name impersonation explicitly as the feature's defining SaaS-operator capability.

features.name: Public status page
features.description: A public page showing current system status, component health, and incident history, with subscriber notifications.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: Cachet (custom non-OSI license) and OpenStatus (AGPL-3.0), both modeling status pages / components / incidents, both reference-only. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Public changelog
features.description: A public or in-app feed of shipped changes and release notes, often paired with an unread-updates indicator.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations found this pass: Chatwoot's in-app changelog feed (app/javascript/dashboard/api/changelog.js, changelog-card components, SidebarChangelogButton.vue with an unread indicator, MIT core) and Twenty CRM's public release-notes page (packages/twenty-website/.../platform/releases/ReleaseNotes.tsx, AGPL, reference-only). The previous boxyhq-saas-starter citation was removed: that repo was checked and confirmed to have no changelog feature, so it was never real evidence. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Enterprise SSO (SAML / OIDC)
features.description: Enterprise single sign-on into a workspace via SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect against the customer's identity provider.

provenance.notes: Implementation (boxyhq's BoxyHQ Jackson SAML integration, lib/jackson) plus both authoritative specs. Verified via `gh api` that Jackson's successor project, Ory Polis (same codebase lineage, Apache-2.0), documents itself as 'an Enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) service for SAML and OIDC identity providers' that 'implements SSO as an OAuth 2.0 flow, abstracting away the complexities of the underlying SAML or OIDC protocol' -- confirming the same integration boxyhq-saas-starter uses genuinely supports OIDC IdPs, not only SAML. OIDC Core is cited here rather than left unused: enterprise SSO in this domain is the tenant-configurable-IdP-federation capability (distinct from shared.auth's basic 'sign in with SSO'/social login), and that capability is protocol-plural in practice. High confidence retained (authoritative source present).

features.name: SCIM provisioning
features.description: Automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning into a workspace from the customer's identity provider via SCIM.

provenance.notes: Implementation (boxyhq Jackson dsync + pages/api/scim/v2.0/[...directory].ts) plus the authoritative SCIM RFC 7643/7644 = high confidence per the brief's rule.

features.name: Self-serve data export
features.description: Let a workspace owner export their tenant's data (CSV/JSON) for backup or portability.

provenance.notes: Twenty CRM has a real, whole-tenant data export implementation: packages/twenty-server/src/database/commands/workspace-export/** (generate-workspace-schema-ddl, build-workspace-table-column-sets, workspace-export.command.ts) — a full-database export per workspace, matching this feature's shape far more closely than the previously-found per-entity CSV export tools. GDPR Article 20 (data portability) remains the authoritative motivation. Raised the single-source medium to a properly two-sourced medium.

features.name: Feature flags
features.description: Toggle features on/off or roll them out gradually, targeted by workspace, user segment, or environment.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: Unleash's FeatureToggle/IFeatureStrategy/IEnvironment model (AGPL-3.0) and Flagsmith's Feature/FeatureSegment/FeatureState/FeatureStateValue model (BSD-3-Clause), both reference-only. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Audit log viewer
features.description: A workspace-scoped UI over the audit log with filters, search, and export, for admins to review who changed what.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: boxyhq's Retraced integration (lib/retraced.ts) and Chatwoot's dashboard audit-log viewer (app/javascript/dashboard/api/auditLogs.js, helper/auditlogHelper.js, MIT core). Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Self-serve billing portal
features.description: Let a workspace owner view invoices, update payment method, and upgrade/downgrade/cancel their subscription.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: boxyhq's Stripe-backed Subscription/Price models and webhook handler, and Twenty CRM's dedicated billing-portal module (billing-portal.workspace-service.ts, stripe-billing-portal.service.ts, useBillingPortalSession.ts) which is literally a Stripe Billing Portal integration. Raised the single-source medium to a properly two-sourced medium.

features.name: Seat management
features.description: Track seats included in a plan, assign/reclaim seats as members are invited or removed, and show pending vs active seat counts.

provenance.notes: boxyhq ties TeamMember to a per-team Subscription; Lago models per-subscription usage/quantity that maps to seat-style metering. Two independent, if partial, sources = medium.

features.name: Custom roles
features.description: Let a workspace define its own roles and permission sets beyond the built-in owner/admin/member roles.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations found this pass: Chatwoot's customRole.js (MIT core) and Twenty CRM's packages/twenty-front/.../settings/roles/** — a full object-level/field-level/row-level custom permission authoring system (AGPL, reference-only). The previous boxyhq-saas-starter citation was removed: that repo only has a fixed ADMIN/MEMBER enum and was cited as a contrasting baseline, not as evidence for this feature. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Trial management
features.description: Time-boxed free trial on a paid plan with expiration handling and trial-to-paid conversion prompts.

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Stripe webhook handler confirms the 'trialing' subscription status at the billing-provider level (partial evidence). Twenty CRM has a full trial flow: billing-trial-ending.email.tsx / billing-trial-converting.email.tsx, billing-trial-period.dto.ts / billing-end-trial-period.dto.ts, and an UpgradeFreeTrial onboarding page (AGPL, reference-only). Two independent sources = medium.

features.name: Workspace deletion with export
features.description: Let a workspace owner delete their workspace, with a data export offer and a grace period before hard deletion, supporting the right to erasure.

provenance.notes: boxyhq implements a DELETE team endpoint (pages/api/teams/[slug]/index.ts); GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure) and CCPA deletion rights are the authoritative motivation for the export-then-purge shape. One implementation + one authoritative source = medium (the implementation alone does not confirm the export-before-purge grace period, which is our inference).

features.name: Public API rate limiting
features.description: Per-key and per-plan request rate limits on the public API, with standard rate-limit response headers.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations found this pass: Chatwoot's config/initializers/rack_attack.rb, which throttles specific API routes per account_id and per API access token (MIT core), and Twenty CRM's engine/core-modules/throttler/** plus usage-limit/utils/build-rate-limit-response-headers.util.ts, which explicitly emits rate-limit response headers (AGPL, reference-only). The previous boxyhq-saas-starter citation was removed: that repo was checked and confirmed to have no rate limiting, so it was never real evidence. Raised low -> medium.

features.name: Sandbox / test environment
features.description: A separate test workspace or API mode with synthetic data, isolated from production, for integration testing.

provenance.notes: Not found in any source inspected this pass; reasoned inference from common developer-tool SaaS practice (e.g. payment-provider test modes), anchored to boxyhq's API-key entity as the mechanism a sandbox key would use. Confidence deliberately low. This pass additionally checked Chatwoot and Twenty CRM (both searched by file tree for 'sandbox'/'test mode') and found no matching tenant sandbox-workspace feature in either. Left at low rather than inventing a second source.

features.name: Data residency controls
features.description: Let an enterprise workspace pin where its data is stored/processed (e.g. EU vs US region) to satisfy jurisdictional requirements.

provenance.notes: Twenty CRM has a real, shipped data-residency control: packages/twenty-shared/src/ai/constants/data-residency.const.ts defines DATA_RESIDENCY_KEYS (us/eu/global/uk/ap/jp/au/ca/de/fr) with a settings UI to select it (MIT sub-package, twenty-shared is one of Twenty's explicitly MIT-licensed packages) — though scoped to the product's AI feature rather than all tenant data, it is direct evidence a per-workspace region-pinning control is a real, buildable pattern, not just a regulatory inference. Combined with the GDPR/ISO 27001 authoritative motivation, raised low -> medium.
